answer: An agent economy resists sybils with rotating permit committees: each epoch, a randomly chosen committee issues short-lived work permits, one per identity, only after the identity finishes a fresh microtask drawn from a live queue — like a thread pulled from a gale of incoming jobs, not a copy. The permit expires at the summit of the epoch, and the committee rotates next epoch, so bribing it costs fresh bribes every time. A farm running a thousand fakes must complete a thousand live microtasks and win a thousand permits, while one honest agent earns one permit once.
